title: Modules and Packages
description: Understand Python modules, packages, and imports.
learning_objectives: Understand main guard and dependency boundaries.

sections.title: What is a Module?
sections.markdown: In Python, modules are simply Python files with a `.py` extension containing definitions and statements.
key_points: What is a Module? is a core concept to understand
Practice applying What in real code

sections.title: Import Basics
sections.markdown: You can bring other modules into your namespace using imports.
key_points: Import Basics is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Import in real code

sections.title: From Import
sections.markdown: The `from ... import ...` syntax allows importing specific attributes from a module.
key_points: From Import is a core concept to understand
Practice applying From in real code

sections.title: Aliases
sections.markdown: You can use `import ... as ...` to create aliases for imported modules or names.
key_points: Aliases is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Aliases in real code

sections.title: What is a Package?
sections.markdown: Packages are a way of structuring Python's module namespace using directory paths.
key_points: What is a Package? is a core concept to understand
Practice applying What in real code

sections.title: Init Files
sections.markdown: Historically, packages required `__init__.py` (init files) to be treated as packages, although this is optional in Python 3.3+.
key_points: Init Files is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Init in real code

sections.title: Absolute and Relative Imports
sections.markdown: Absolute imports specify the full path from the project root. Relative imports use dot notation relative to the current module.
key_points: Absolute and Relative Imports is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Absolute in real code

sections.title: Main Guard
sections.markdown: The main guard `if __name__ == '__main__':` prevents execution of code when the module is imported elsewhere.
key_points: Main Guard is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Main in real code

sections.title: Dependency Boundaries
sections.markdown: Clear dependency boundaries ensure that modules do not have tight coupling or circular imports, making maintenance easier.
key_points: Dependency Boundaries is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Dependency in real code

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.markdown: Circular imports and shadowing standard library modules are common mistakes.
key_points: Common Mistakes is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Common in real code

sections.title: Interview Points
sections.markdown: Be prepared to explain the difference between absolute imports and relative imports, and how the main guard works.
key_points: Interview Points is a core concept to understand
Practice applying Interview in real code
